newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Gazprom, UES to remain intact - PM.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Gazprom, UES to remain intact - PM.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin repeated assurances on Tuesday that natural monopolies like national power company UES and natural gas producer Gazprom would not be broken up.

Chernomyrdin told Energy Ministry officials that government efforts to revamp the natural monopolies, large companies with no competition such as gas and power producers, would focus on strengthening them.
"All that we are going to do in this sphere is strengthen the existing energy system," Interfax news agency quoted Chernomyrdin as saying.
President Boris Yeltsin signed a decree last week ordering the government to draw up plans for restructuring, privatising and strengthening state control of the natural monopolies.
First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov, recently appointed Minister of Fuel and Energy, is leading the government campaign.

But he faces opposition from many quarters, including the Russian parliament and the companies involved, who have spoken out against the breakup of the monopolies, despite many government statements that the companies will remain intact.
